## nexuml_library.data.audioset.audioset.AudiosetDataset

*class*

```python
class AudiosetDataset(DataSourceDefinition)
```

Bases: `DataSourceDefinition`

AudioSet dataset source.

Scans <data_dir> for .wav or .npy files. File names must encode labels
via the pattern ``<ytid>__<label_str>.<ext>`` where label_str is
underscore-joined AudioSet display names.

A cached metadata CSV is read/written to ``<meta_dir>/<data_dir.name>_meta.csv``
so subsequent loads are fast.

Label columns: class (int index), class_logits (multi-hot list).

**Attributes**

- `data_dir` (`str | Path`) — Directory containing audio/feature files.
- `meta_dir` (`str | Path`) — Directory for class_labels_indices.csv and the cached meta CSV.
- `perform_checks` (`bool`) — Whether to verify each file is loadable (slow on first run).
- `len_seconds` (`float`) — Minimum audio duration in seconds to include a file.
- `sample_rate` (`int`) — Target sample rate for audio loading.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/audioset/audioset.py#L89-L117)

## nexuml_library.data.audioset.audioset_hf_download.download_hf_audioset

*function*

```python
def download_hf_audioset(root: str | Path, decode: bool = True) -> None
```

Download AudioSet from Hugging Face into ``root``.

Uses only ``agkphysics/AudioSet`` config ``full`` and splits
``bal_train``, ``eval``, and ``unbal_train``. No YouTube or yt-dlp code is
imported or invoked.

**Raises**

- `RuntimeError` — If required packages (datasets, torchaudio, tqdm)
are not installed.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/audioset/audioset_hf_download.py#L33-L106)

# nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026

*module*

DCASE 2026 dataset sources for Tasks 1, 2, and 7.

All datasets are metadata-backed and fake-fixture friendly: they accept
pre-built DataFrames and tiny local audio files for testing without
requiring network downloads.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/dcaset2/dcase2026.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026.DCASE2026T1Dataset

*class*

```python
class DCASE2026T1Dataset(DataSourceDefinition)
```

Bases: `DataSourceDefinition`

DCASE 2026 Task 1 dataset for BSD10k-v1.2 / BSD35k-CS.

Expects a metadata CSV with columns including at least:
``file``, ``sound_id``, ``class_top``, ``class_second``.
Optional columns: ``confidence``, ``uploader``, ``license``, ``title``,
``tags``, ``description``, ``clap_embedding``.

**Attributes**

- `root` (`str | Path`) — Dataset root directory.
- `metadata_csv` (`str`) — Path to metadata CSV relative to root.
- `download_mode` (`DownloadMode`) — One of the DownloadMode literals.
- `checksum` (`str | None`) — Optional expected checksum of the metadata CSV.
- `clap_embeddings_dir` (`str | None`) — Optional directory with pre-computed CLAP .npy files.
- `fold_seed` (`int`) — Seed for reproducible baseline 5-fold splits.
- `fold_id` (`int | None`) — If provided, filter to that fold (0-4).
- `split` (`str`) — ``"fit"``, ``"val"``, ``"test"``, or ``"eval"``.
- `sample_rate` (`int`) — Target audio sample rate.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/dcaset2/dcase2026.py#L725-L758)

## nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026.DCASE2026T2Dataset

*class*

```python
class DCASE2026T2Dataset(DCASET2Dataset)
```

Bases: `nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026.DCASET2Dataset`

DCASE 2026 Task 2 dataset — metadata index with domain/attribute enrichment.

Extends ``DCASET2Dataset`` with 2026-specific metadata:
- ``domain`` inferred from filename source/target markers
- ``attributes`` merged from the official attributes CSV when available

Audio is 2-channel (stereo). Channel selection happens in pipeline layers,
not here. DALI loads raw stereo audio as [C, T] via ``dali_layout="CT"``.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/dcaset2/dcase2026.py#L944-L960)

## nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026.DCASE2026T7Dataset

*class*

```python
class DCASE2026T7Dataset(DataSourceDefinition)
```

Bases: `DataSourceDefinition`

DCASE 2026 Task 7 DIL-DCASE26 dataset.

Expects a root directory with subfolders ``D2/`` and ``D3/`` (and
optionally ``D1/`` for baseline reference).  Each domain folder may
contain:

- ``metadata.csv`` with columns ``file``, ``class``, ``domain``
- Raw audio files (optionally with ``evaluation_setup/`` split files)

The dataset exposes a sequence-of-increments interface via
``get_increment()``.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/dcaset2/dcase2026.py#L1179-L1203)

## nexuml_library.data.dcaset2.dcase2026.DCASET2Dataset

*class*

```python
class DCASET2Dataset(DataSourceDefinition)
```

Bases: `DataSourceDefinition`

DCASE Task 2 anomalous sound detection dataset.

Builds a metadata DataFrame from the DCASE directory structure and
lazily loads audio/features in load_item().

> **Directory layout expected**
>
> <root>/<dataset_name>/<data_type>_data/raw/<machine_type>/train/
> <root>/<dataset_name>/<data_type>_data/raw/<machine_type>/test/

> **machine (int index), y_true (0=normal,1=anomalous),**
>
> condition (int), target (0/1).

**Attributes**

- `root` (`str | Path | None`) — Path to the dataset root directory.
- `dataset_name` (`str`) — e.g. "DCASE2024T2"
- `machine_type` (`str`) — e.g. "ToyCar", "fan", etc.
- `section_keyword` (`str`) — prefix for section names, e.g. "section"
- `section_ids` (`list[str] | None`) — list of section id strings, e.g. ["00", "01"]
- `data_type` (`str`) — "dev" or "eval"
- `train` (`bool`) — if True load train split, else test split
- `sample_rate` (`int`) — target sample rate for audio loading
- `machine_types` (`list[str] | None`) — list of all machine types (for machine index mapping)

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/dcaset2/dcase2026.py#L129-L172)

# nexuml_library.data.synthetic

*module*

Synthetic dataset for testing architectures without real data.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/synthetic.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.data.synthetic.SyntheticDataset

*class*

```python
class SyntheticDataset(DataSourceDefinition)
```

Bases: `DataSourceDefinition`

Universal synthetic tensor dataset for architecture testing.

Generates arbitrary feature tensors with optional targets:
- reconstruction (features are their own target)
- multiclass labels (from cluster assignments)
- multilabel labels (random binary vectors)
- multi-output regression targets (linear combination + noise)

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/data/synthetic.py#L30-L50)

# nexuml_library.evaluation.anomalous_sound_detection.asd_evaluator

*module*

Composable ASD reporting eval algorithms: AnomalyEvaluator and AnomalyVisualizer.

Score-producing components (GroupDistancePipelineLayer, ScoreCalibrationPipelineLayer,
ScoreReductionPipelineLayer, DecisionRulePipelineLayer) are now in
nexuml_library.layers.head as PostTrainFitLayer subclasses.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/evaluation/anomalous_sound_detection/asd_evaluator.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.evaluation.anomalous_sound_detection.asd_evaluator.AnomalyEvaluator

*class*

```python
class AnomalyEvaluator(EvalAlgorithmDefinition)
```

Bases: `EvalAlgorithmDefinition`

Reporting algorithm: computes AUC, pAUC, and DCASE metrics.

Reads anomaly_score from the pipeline output TensorDict. Does not produce
any score keys — score production is handled by pipeline layers.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/evaluation/anomalous_sound_detection/asd_evaluator.py#L74-L95)

## nexuml_library.evaluation.anomalous_sound_detection.decision.DecisionRule

*class*

```python
class DecisionRule(nn.Module)
```

Bases: `nn.Module`

Abstract decision rule.

> **Lifecycle**
>
> 1. fit(train_scores) — fit threshold from normal train scores
> 2. forward(scores) -> decisions — apply threshold to produce binary decisions

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/evaluation/anomalous_sound_detection/decision.py#L15-L37)

*class*

```python
class LatentVisualizer(EvalAlgorithmDefinition)
```

Bases: `EvalAlgorithmDefinition`

Visualizes latent space using t-SNE or UMAP projection.

Uses reservoir sampling to handle large datasets efficiently.
Train and test samples are projected together and colored by label/split.

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.L2Normalize

*class*

```python
class L2Normalize(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Re-exported from: `nexuml_library.layers.feature.l2_normalize`

L2-normalize the last dimension of the input.

Stateless — no trainable parameters and no fitted state. Equivalent
to ``torch.nn.functional.normalize(x, p=2, dim=-1, eps=eps)``.

**Attributes**

- `eps` (`float`) — Small epsilon added to the denominator to avoid division by zero. Defaults to ``1e-12`` (matches ``F.normalize`` default).

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/l2_normalize.py#L24-L39)

# nexuml_library.layers.feature.l2_normalize

*module*

L2-normalization pipeline layer.

A trivial stateless postproc: applies L2 normalization to the last
dimension of the input. Has no trainable state and no ``fit()``/``is_fitted``
contract — it is an ordinary pipeline composition primitive, not a
train-fitted postprocessor.

This is the canonical "normalize embeddings" step the DCASE 2026 P3
target pipeline uses. It is intentionally a separate layer from
:class:`FeaturePostproc` so the target scenario does not need a
train-fitted postproc / pre-materialization bridge contract.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/l2_normalize.py#L1-L1)

# nexuml_library.layers.feature.lmbe

*module*

Log Mel Band Energy (LMBE) feature extractor layer.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/lmbe.py#L1-L1)


[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/lmbe.py#L13-L13)

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.lmbe.LMBE

*class*

```python
class LMBE(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Compute Log Mel Band Energies from a raw waveform.

Uses torchaudio's MelSpectrogram + AmplitudeToDB pipeline.
Optionally falls back to librosa for compatibility.

**Attributes**

- `n_mels` (`int`) — Number of Mel filterbanks.
- `n_fft` (`int`) — FFT size.
- `hop_length` (`int`) — Number of samples between frames.
- `win_length` (`int | None`) — Window length in samples.
- `power` (`int`) — Spectrogram power (1=magnitude, 2=power).
- `fmin` (`int`) — Minimum frequency.
- `fmax` (`int`) — Maximum frequency.
- `sr` (`int`) — Sample rate.
- `mel_scale` (`str`) — Mel scale type ("slaney" or "htk").
- `pad_mode` (`str`) — Padding mode for STFT.
- `use_librosa` (`bool`) — Use librosa backend instead of torchaudio.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/lmbe.py#L16-L52)

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.AttentionPool

*class*

```python
class AttentionPool(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Learned attention pooling using a query token.

**Attributes**

- `remove_dim` (`bool`) — Whether to remove the pooled dimension.
- `n_heads` (`int`) — Number of attention heads.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/pooling.py#L184-L199)

### nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.AttentionPool.dim

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.AttentiveStatisticsPool

```python
class AttentiveStatisticsPool(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Attentive Statistics Pooling (Okabe et al., 2018).

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.TokenPool

*class*

```python
class TokenPool(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Pool tokens along a specified dimension.

**Attributes**

- `dim` (`int`) — Dimension to pool over (negative indexing supported, e.g. -2 for time).
- `pooling_type` (`Literal['mean', 'max', 'std', 'mean_std', 'cls', 'multilayer']`) — - "mean": average over the pool dim - "max": max over the pool dim - "std": standard deviation over the pool dim - "mean_std" (alias: "mean+std", "mean_plus_std"): concatenate   mean and std along the last axis - "cls": select the first index along the pool dim (CLS-style) - "multilayer": when the input is multi-layer hidden states   (e.g. ``[B, L, N, D]`` from an encoder that exposes all   hidden states), concatenate per-layer mean+std along the   last axis, preserving the per-layer ordering.
- `remove_dim` (`bool`) — Whether to squeeze the pooled dimension.
- `skip_first` (`bool`) — Skip the first token (e.g. CLS token) before pooling.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/pooling.py#L21-L48)

### nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.TokenPool.dim

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
dim: int = -2
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/pooling.py#L42-L42)

### nexuml_library.layers.feature.pooling.TokenPool.pooling_type

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
pooling_type: Literal['mean', 'max', 'std', 'mean_std', 'cls', 'multilayer'] = 'mean'
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/pooling.py#L43-L43)

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/pooling.py#L44-L44)

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.projector.Conv1dProjector

*class*

```python
class Conv1dProjector(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Pointwise Conv1d projector for sequence inputs (B, T, C).

Equivalent to Linear but uses Conv1d for better memory access patterns.

**Attributes**

- `target_dim` (`int | None`) — Output channel dimension. If None, uses output_sizes.
- `hidden_dim` (`int`) — Hidden size for multi-layer projectors.
- `n_layers` (`int`) — Number of projection layers.
- `bias` (`bool`) — Whether to use bias.
- `activation` (`str | None`) — Dotted class path for activation.
- `normalization` (`str | None`) — Dotted class path for normalization.

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.projector.Linear

*class*

```python
class Linear(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Multi-layer linear projector with optional activation and normalization.

**Attributes**

- `target_dim` (`int | None`) — Output dimension. If None, uses output_sizes.
- `hidden_dim` (`int`) — Hidden layer size (for n_layers > 1).
- `hidden_dims` (`list[int] | None`) — Explicit hidden-layer sizes. When provided, overrides hidden_dim/n_layers for layer construction.
- `n_layers` (`int`) — Number of linear layers.
- `linear_bias` (`bool`) — Whether to use bias.
- `activation` (`str | None`) — Dotted class path, e.g. "torch.nn.GELU".
- `normalization` (`str | None`) — Dotted class path, e.g. "torch.nn.BatchNorm1d".
- `skip_last_activation` (`bool`) — Skip activation after the last layer.
- `flatten_dims` (`tuple[int, int] | None`) — Optional (start, end) dims to flatten before projection.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/projector.py#L34-L62)

## nexuml_library.layers.feature.projector.LowRankProjector

*class*

```python
class LowRankProjector(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Low-rank factorized projection W ≈ U @ V.

Reduces parameters from O(C*D) to O((C+D)*r) when r << min(C, D).

**Attributes**

- `target_dim` (`int | None`) — Output dimension. If None, uses output_sizes.
- `rank` (`int`) — Bottleneck rank.
- `bias` (`bool`) — Whether to use bias.
- `activation` (`str | None`) — Optional activation between U and V.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/feature/projector.py#L204-L223)

# nexuml_library.layers.loss.classification_metrics

*module*

Classification metrics layer.

Supports both multiclass and multilabel classification metrics via the
``multi_label`` flag.  In multilabel mode, sigmoid is applied to logits
before updating metrics and labels are kept as multi-hot vectors.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/loss/classification_metrics.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.layers.loss.classification_metrics.ClassificationMetrics

*class*

```python
class ClassificationMetrics(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Accumulate classification metrics with torchmetrics.

When ``multi_label`` is ``False`` (default) the layer uses multiclass
metrics (``MulticlassAccuracy``, ``MulticlassF1Score``,
``MulticlassAveragePrecision``).  Labels are expected as integer class
indices with shape ``[batch]``.

When ``multi_label`` is ``True`` the layer uses multilabel metrics
(``MultilabelAccuracy``, ``MultilabelF1Score``,
``MultilabelAveragePrecision``).  Sigmoid is applied to logits before
passing them to the metrics and labels are expected as multi-hot float
tensors with shape ``[batch, num_labels]``.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/loss/classification_metrics.py#L21-L49)

### nexuml_library.layers.loss.classification_metrics.ClassificationMetrics.average

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
average: str = 'macro'
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/loss/classification_metrics.py#L38-L38)

### nexuml_library.layers.loss.classification_metrics.ClassificationMetrics.metrics

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
metrics: list[str] | None = None
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/loss/classification_metrics.py#L37-L37)

```python
multi_label: bool = False
```

# nexuml_library.layers.loss.multilabel_map_metrics

*module*

Multi-label mAP metric layer.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/loss/multilabel_map_metrics.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.layers.loss.multilabel_map_metrics.MultiLabelMAPMetrics

*class*

```python
class MultiLabelMAPMetrics(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

Pipeline layer computing multi-label mean Average Precision.

Consumes logits from keys_in[0] and multi-hot labels from y[label_key].
Applies sigmoid to logits before updating the wrapped
torchmetrics MultilabelAveragePrecision metric.

## nexuml_library.layers.model.resnet.ResNet

*class*

```python
class ResNet(LayerDefinition)
```

Bases: `LayerDefinition`

ResNet backbone that emits feature embeddings.

Wraps ``torchvision.models.resnet*`` and replaces the final
fully-connected layer with an identity so downstream heads
can operate on embeddings.

**Attributes**

- `resnet_type` (`ResNetType`) — Architecture variant (e.g. ``"resnet18"``).
- `pretrained` (`bool`) — Whether to load pretrained ImageNet weights.
- `cifar_stem` (`bool | None`) — Use a CIFAR-friendly stem (3x3 stride-1, no maxpool). Defaults to ``False`` when pretrained, ``True`` otherwise.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/model/resnet.py#L20-L40)

### nexuml_library.layers.model.resnet.ResNet.cifar_stem

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
cifar_stem: bool | None = None
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/model/resnet.py#L37-L37)

### nexuml_library.layers.model.resnet.ResNet.pretrained

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
pretrained: bool = False
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/layers/model/resnet.py#L36-L36)

### nexuml_library.layers.model.resnet.ResNet.resnet_type

*attribute* · *class attribute* · *instance attribute*

```python
resnet_type: ResNetType = 'resnet18'
```

## nexuml_library.scenarios.asd.audioset_conv_ae_clshead.audioset_conv_ae_clshead

*function*

```python
def audioset_conv_ae_clshead(data_root: str = 'audioset_hf/full', download: bool = False, sample_rate: int = 16000, clip_num_samples: int = 160000, n_mels: int = 128, hop_length: int = 512, latent_dim: int = 64, channel_schedule: list[int] | None = None, num_classes: int = 527, lr: float = 0.001, batch_size: int = 128, max_epochs: int = 10, validate_layout: bool = False) -> ScenarioSpec
```

Conv AE trained on AudioSet waveforms with reconstruction + classification.

A ``LatentClassificationHead`` is added on top of the encoder latent space,
and both reconstruction and classification losses are optimized jointly.

# nexuml_library.scenarios.asd.dcase_conv_ae_baseline

*module*

DCASE convolutional autoencoder scenarios.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/asd/dcase_conv_ae_baseline.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.asd.dcase_conv_ae_baseline.dcase_conv_ae

*function*

```python
def dcase_conv_ae(machine_types: list[str] | None = None, machine_specs: list[MachineSpec] | None = None, download: bool = False, n_mels: int = 128, hop_length: int = 512, clip_num_samples: int = 160000, latent_dim: int = 64, channel_schedule: list[int] | None = None, lr: float = 0.001, batch_size: int = 16, max_epochs: int = 25) -> ScenarioSpec
```

DCASE convolutional autoencoder anomaly workflow.

Machine year and data_type come from the built-in DCASE catalog when
``machine_types`` is given. Use ``machine_specs`` for explicit multi-year
control. ``time_frames`` is computed from ``clip_num_samples / hop_length``.

**Returns**

- `ScenarioSpec` (`ScenarioSpec`) — Assembled scenario with pipeline, training, data and evaluation.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/asd/dcase_conv_ae_baseline.py#L15-L64)


DCASE convolutional variational autoencoder anomaly workflow.

Machine year and data_type come from the built-in DCASE catalog when
``machine_types`` is given. ``time_frames`` is computed automatically.

```python
DCASE_MACHINE_SPECS: tuple[MachineSpec, ...] = tuple((MachineSpec(machine_type=machine_type, year=year, data_type=data_type) for year, data_types in _DCASE_MACHINES.items() for data_type, machine_types in data_types.items() for machine_type in machine_types))
```

```python
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
```

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/data/dcase.py#L14-L14)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.data.dcase.MachineSpec

*class* · *pydantic model*

```python
class MachineSpec(BaseModel)
```

Bases: `BaseModel`

Identifies a DCASE machine type together with the year it was released.

The year determines which dataset subdirectory the files live in
(e.g. year=2023 → ``dcase2023t2/``).  ``data_type`` is either
``"dev"`` (labelled development set) or ``"eval"`` (evaluation set).

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/data/dcase.py#L17-L36)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.data.dcase.dcase_data

*function*

```python
def dcase_data(data_root: str | Path = 'DCASET2', machine_types: list[str] | None = None, machine_specs: list[MachineSpec] | None = None, train_machine_specs: list[MachineSpec] | None = None, test_machine_specs: list[MachineSpec] | None = None, years: list[int] | None = None, data_types: list[str] | None = None, dedupe_machine_types: bool = False, download: bool = False, sample_rate: int = 16000, clip_num_samples: int = 160000, batch_size: int = 64, num_workers: int = 4, validate_machine_specs: bool = True) -> DataSpec
```

DCASE Task 2 anomaly detection data spec.

Pass ``machine_specs`` for explicit multi-year control, or ``machine_types``
to filter the built-in DCASE machine catalog.

Set ``NEXUML_DATA_ROOT`` so scenario files can use logical dataset
paths without cluster-specific paths in code.

**Parameters**

- `data_root` (`str | Path`) (default: `'DCASET2'`) — Logical root. Resolved via ``NEXUML_DATA_ROOT`` if the path does not exist as-is.
- `machine_types` (`list[str] | None`) (default: `None`) — Names of machine types to keep from the catalog.
- `machine_specs` (`list[MachineSpec] | None`) (default: `None`) — Explicit per-machine year + data_type (multi-year) for both fit and test.
- `train_machine_specs` (`list[MachineSpec] | None`) (default: `None`) — Explicit machine specs used only for fit.
- `test_machine_specs` (`list[MachineSpec] | None`) (default: `None`) — Explicit machine specs used only for test.
- `years` (`list[int] | None`) (default: `None`) — Optional year filter.
- `data_types` (`list[str] | None`) (default: `None`) — Optional data type filter, e.g. ["eval"] for additional/eval machines.
- `dedupe_machine_types` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — Keep at most one spec per raw machine type, preferring eval/newer year.
- `download` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — Download/extract missing Zenodo zips from the DCASE manifest.
- `sample_rate` (`int`) (default: `16000`) — Audio sample rate in Hz.
- `clip_num_samples` (`int`) (default: `160000`) — Samples per audio clip.
- `batch_size` (`int`) (default: `64`) — DataLoader batch size.
- `num_workers` (`int`) (default: `4`) — DataLoader workers.
- `validate_machine_specs` (`bool`) (default: `True`) — Validate explicit machine_specs against the catalog. Set to False to allow custom/experimental machines not in the catalog.

**Returns**

- `DataSpec` (`DataSpec`) — DCASE dataset specification with fit and test splits.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/data/dcase.py#L187-L344)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.data.dcase.dcase_machine_specs

*function*

```python
def dcase_machine_specs(machine_types: list[str] | None = None, years: list[int] | None = None, data_types: list[str] | None = None, dedupe_machine_types: bool = False) -> list[MachineSpec]
```

Return known DCASE machine specs from the static scenario catalog.

When ``dedupe_machine_types`` is true, keep at most one spec per raw machine
type, preferring eval over dev and newer years over older years.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/data/dcase.py#L151-L184)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.data.roots.resolve_data_root

*function*

```python
def resolve_data_root(data_root: str, env_var: str = 'NEXUML_DATA_ROOT') -> Path
```

Resolve a dataset path against the optional global data root.

Absolute paths are used as-is. Relative paths are resolved under
``NEXUML_DATA_ROOT`` when set. Otherwise, relative paths are returned
unchanged and remain relative to the current working directory.

**Returns**

- `Path` (`Path`) — Resolved dataset path.

```python
def anomaly_evaluation_spec(label_key: str = 'anomaly', group_keys: list[str] | None = None, output_score_key: str = 'anomaly_score', decision_key: str | None = 'decision', dcase_metric_axes: dict[str, str] | None = None, max_fpr: float = 0.1) -> EvaluationSpec
```

Evaluation-only spec for anomalous sound detection.

Returns only the reporting algorithm (anomaly_evaluator). Score-producing
components (group_distance, calibration, reduction) are pipeline layers.

**Returns**

- `EvaluationSpec` (`EvaluationSpec`) — Evaluation specification with anomaly evaluator algorithm.

## nexuml_library.scenarios.evaluation.anomaly.classification_metrics_spec

*function*

```python
def classification_metrics_spec(score_key: str = 'anomaly_score', decision_key: str = 'decision', label_key: str = 'anomaly', metrics: list[str] | None = None, fit_mask_key: str | None = None, fit_label_key: str | None = None) -> dict[str, list[LayerSpec]]
```

Return a pipeline stage dict containing a decision rule and ``ClassificationMetrics``.

## nexuml_library.scenarios.model.linear_ae.linear_ae_reconstruction

- Loss: ClassificationLoss + ClassificationMetrics

# nexuml_library.scenarios.vision.cifar_resnet

*module*

Composed CIFAR + ResNet classification scenarios.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/vision/cifar_resnet.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.scenarios.vision.cifar_resnet.cifar_resnet

*function*

```python
def cifar_resnet(dataset: str = 'cifar10', download: bool = True, resnet_type: ResNetType = 'resnet18', pretrained: bool = False, cifar_stem: bool | None = None, lr: float = 0.001, batch_size: int = 64, max_epochs: int = 10) -> ScenarioSpec
```

CIFAR image classification with ResNet backbone.

**Parameters**

- `dataset` (`str`) (default: `'cifar10'`) — ``"cifar10"`` or ``"cifar100"``.
- `download` (`bool`) (default: `True`) — Auto-download dataset if not present.
- `resnet_type` (`ResNetType`) (default: `'resnet18'`) — ResNet variant (e.g. ``"resnet18"``).
- `pretrained` (`bool`) (default: `False`) — Load pretrained ImageNet weights.
- `cifar_stem` (`bool | None`) (default: `None`) — Use CIFAR-friendly stem. Defaults to ``True`` when ``pretrained=False``.
- `lr` (`float`) (default: `0.001`) — Learning rate.
- `batch_size` (`int`) (default: `64`) — Training batch size.
- `max_epochs` (`int`) (default: `10`) — Maximum training epochs.

**Returns**

- `ScenarioSpec` (`ScenarioSpec`) — Assembled scenario with pipeline, training, data and evaluation.

**Raises**

- `ValueError` — If ``dataset`` is not ``"cifar10"`` or ``"cifar100"``.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/scenarios/vision/cifar_resnet.py#L23-L86)

## nexuml_library.training.WarmupCosineLR

*class*

```python
class WarmupCosineLR(torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler)
```

Bases: `torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler`

Re-exported from: `nexuml_library.training.schedulers.warmup_cosine`

Linear warmup followed by cosine decay to an absolute LR floor.

**Parameters**

- `optimizer` (`torch.optim.Optimizer`) — Optimizer whose parameter groups will be scheduled.
- `warmup_epochs` (`int`) — Number of initial epochs spent linearly increasing from ``min_lr`` to ``base_lr``. Use ``0`` to disable warmup.
- `max_epochs` (`int`) — Total scheduler horizon. At ``epoch == max_epochs`` the LR is ``min_lr``.
- `min_lr` (`float`) — Absolute minimum learning rate, not a multiplier.
- `last_epoch` (`int`) (default: `-1`) — Last scheduler epoch, forwarded to PyTorch's scheduler base.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/training/schedulers/warmup_cosine.py#L10-L63)

### nexuml_library.training.WarmupCosineLR.max_epochs


[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/training/schedulers/warmup_cosine.py#L46-L46)

### nexuml_library.training.WarmupCosineLR.min_lr

```python
min_lr = min_lr
```

# nexuml_library.training.schedulers.warmup_cosine

*module*

Learning-rate schedulers for NexuML library scenarios.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/training/schedulers/warmup_cosine.py#L1-L1)

## nexuml_library.training.schedulers.warmup_cosine.WarmupCosineLR

*class*

```python
class WarmupCosineLR(torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler)
```

Bases: `torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LRScheduler`

Linear warmup followed by cosine decay to an absolute LR floor.

**Parameters**

- `optimizer` (`torch.optim.Optimizer`) — Optimizer whose parameter groups will be scheduled.
- `warmup_epochs` (`int`) — Number of initial epochs spent linearly increasing from ``min_lr`` to ``base_lr``. Use ``0`` to disable warmup.
- `max_epochs` (`int`) — Total scheduler horizon. At ``epoch == max_epochs`` the LR is ``min_lr``.
- `min_lr` (`float`) — Absolute minimum learning rate, not a multiplier.
- `last_epoch` (`int`) (default: `-1`) — Last scheduler epoch, forwarded to PyTorch's scheduler base.

[View source](https://github.com/NexuFed/NexuML/blob/f54bedddeadd6bea3168c52441dc09bb2d77a22b/library/src/nexuml_library/training/schedulers/warmup_cosine.py#L10-L63)
